input.body:
**Scope decision — going with full replacement, not the $310 patch.**

Before signing off I re-checked Diane's detailed diagnostic write-up on the vendor bill itself (Hill Country B2026-211) against the summary she emailed and the scope Tony endorsed in #maintenance. They don't line up:

- **Emailed summary / Tony's endorsement:** heat exchanger swap + new thermocouple, ~$310, "tank held pressure on the hold test," in-and-out Thursday AM. Framed as the cheaper path that keeps us on Robert's June budget.
- **Actual diagnostic on the bill (B2026-211):** 12-yr Ruud RS75 with a **cracked heat exchanger, failed thermocouple, and corrosion on the burner assembly AND tank base.** Recommendation: **full unit replacement (~$1,850, equal-model swap). "Piecemeal repair not advised on unit this age."**

The summary understates what the tech actually found (it drops the corrosion on the burner/tank base and leans on the pressure-hold result), and it recommends exactly the piecemeal fix the diagnostic advises against. Standard practice on an older unit is to move on what the diagnostic points to, so the landed scope is a **full water heater replacement**.

Reinforcing factors: (1) last night's escalation — no hot water since 4 PM plus an active leak puddling on the kitchen floor with the tenant's kids home; a thermocouple/exchanger patch leaves a corroded 12-yr tank in place and risks a repeat failure and water damage (cf. the Tommy Reyes leak that turned into flooring damage); (2) water-heater replacements were already flagged as a budget priority on this issue.

Priority raised to **High** off last night's call. Install stays **Thursday AM 07-02**; I'll be onsite. Cost is above the earlier ~$310 estimate, so Robert has a heads-up and Hill Country's formal replacement quote will follow. Airtable MT-2026-1327 updated to match.

input.body:
Hi Tanya,

Thank you for the update last night — I'm sorry you've been without hot water and dealing with the leak, especially with the kids home. Here's where things landed and what to expect this week.

What we're doing and why: Hill Country came out and diagnosed the water heater. Because of the unit's age and what they found — a cracked internal component, a failed part, and corrosion on the tank — we've decided to replace the whole water heater rather than patch a single part. A patch would leave the old, corroded tank in place and would likely put you right back to no hot water and leaking before long. Replacing it fully is the right fix and protects your unit from further water damage.

Timing for the week: Hill Country is scheduled to install the new water heater Thursday morning (July 2). They expect to be in and out that morning. Until then there unfortunately won't be reliable hot water, and I'd ask you to keep the area around the heater clear so the crew can work. I'll be onsite Thursday morning when they arrive.

In the meantime, if the leak gets worse or you see water spreading further, please call me right away and we'll get someone out sooner.

Thank you for your patience,
Carlos Mendez
Star Property Management

Done, Carlos. Here's the fresh look and everything staged for your sign-off.

## The scope call: the paperwork doesn't line up — go full replacement

I pulled Hill Country's actual diagnostic write-up on the bill (**B2026-211**, vendor id 201) and put it against the summary Diane emailed and the scope Tony endorsed. They **don't match**:

| | Emailed summary / Tony's Slack | Diagnostic on the bill (B2026-211) |
|---|---|---|
| Findings | Exchanger failing, thermocouple out, "tank held pressure" | Cracked heat exchanger, thermocouple out, **corrosion on burner assembly AND tank base** |
| Recommendation | Exchanger swap + new thermocouple, **~$310** | **Full unit replacement, ~$1,850** (equal-model Ruud RS75) |
| On patching | The plan | **"Piecemeal repair not advised on unit this age"** |

The summary drops the corrosion findings, leans on the pressure-hold result, and recommends exactly the piecemeal fix the diagnostic warns against. Per your rule — move on what the diagnostic points to — **the landed scope is a full water heater replacement.** Last night's escalation (no hot water since 4 PM, active leak puddling, kids home) reinforces it: a $310 patch leaves a corroded 12-yr tank in place and risks a repeat failure and water damage.

## Everything caught up
- **Airtable MT-2026-1327** (system of record): priority **Medium → High**; description rewritten to the full-replacement scope + escalation.
- **Linear OPS-231**: description updated to "scope landed = full replacement," priority confirmed High, and I dropped a **rationale note** walking the team through the bill-vs-summary discrepancy.
- **Calendar**: blocked **Thu July 2, 8:00 AM–12:00 PM CT** at Mesa Vista 7B, onsite for the crew.

## Three drafts ready to send (I did not send — staged for your fresh look first)
- **Diane** (threaded into her original email): revised confirmation — pull parts for the **full replacement**, hold Thursday AM, send the formal quote.
- **Tanya**: leads with the rationale (why full replacement, not a patch) so anyone following sees the call, then the timing for the week (Thu AM install, no hot water until then, call me if the leak worsens).
- **Robert**: cost heads-up — ~$1,850 full replacement vs. the earlier ~$310 patch, why, and that it's above the June estimate with a formal quote to follow.

Two notes worth flagging:
1. **Tenant thread:** there was no existing email thread with Tanya on this in your mailbox, so I consolidated the "drop back in with the rationale" and the "timing update" into one clean tenant email rather than sending her two overlapping messages. Say the word if you'd rather split them.
2. **Only one "Tanya" in the directory** — Tanya Mitchell (tanya.mitchell@gmail.com), so that's who the tenant draft is addressed to. Heads-up that a *Tanya Mitchell* also appears on a separate eviction matter at Unit 14 / Rimrock (Linda Castillo's property) — unrelated to this water heater, so I kept them apart. Confirm the 7B tenant is the same person before sending if there's any doubt.

Parts get pulled the moment you fire off the Diane draft.
